title: TS-ICL: A Flexible Time-Indexed Foundation Model for Time Series via In-Context Learning
claim: A multi-stage modular pipeline turns raw timestamps and values into context-aware representations, then regresses targets in-context.
layout: 4 numbered dashed panels, left-to-right, top then bottom, tensor shapes under blocks
description: A four-panel block diagram with dashed borders, numbered 1–4. Panel 1 is the Time Series Encoder. It shows the look-back and horizon timelines, with green covariate points and red context points. Learnable tokens go through blocks for encoding coordinates, aggregating values and self-attention. Stacks of red and green token bars show the data after each step. Panel 2 is the Task-oriented Channel Mixer. It uses cross-attention to turn channel-independent representations into covariate-aware ones. It then reshapes and applies self-attention to give the final representation. Panel 3 is the Temporal Context Query Module. A query timestamp is turned into a frequency embedding and cross-attends to the final representation to give H(t). Panel 4 is the In-Context Learning Regressor. Training tuples are blue and target tokens are yellow. Colored arcs show causal self-attention, and quantile regression produces the predictions. Tensor shapes in math notation sit under each block.
caption: The TS-ICL pipeline. From temporal encoding to in-context regression. The diagram illustrates the four-module transformation for forecasting with one covariate observed on the horizon.
abstract: Foundation models mark a profound paradigm shift in time series modeling, with task-specific models being superseded by general-purpose zero-shot models. Yet, current approaches primarily focus on forecasting, while real-world time series are often irregularly and partially observed, requiring models that can jointly forecast, impute missing values, and handle degraded sampling conditions. To address these challenges, we introduce TS-ICL, a novel probabilistic In-Context Learning encoder--regressor Transformer that unifies forecasting and imputation. TS-ICL formulates time series tasks as timestamp-aligned regression and naturally incorporates covariates by training on synthetic dependency structures generated from a novel causal data prior. Empirically, TS-ICL achieves a new state-of-the-art in imputation, while remaining competitive with leading forecasting foundation models across both univariate and covariate-aware benchmarks. It shows particularly strong performance in forecasting with partially observed look-back windows.
